actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: Adroit is a 28 degree of freedom system: a 24 degree of freedom ShadowHand and a 4 degree of freedom arm
The Adroit platform is tendon-driven and pneumatically actuated; the README describes the hand as a system with 24 degrees of freedom and 40 tendons
Adroit_hand.xml includes resources/assets.xml and resources/joint_position_actuation.xml; the tendon torque actuation include is commented out
The model's <option> element sets the physics timestep to 0.002 s
The hand mount body at the world origin includes resources/chain.xml and declares no joint of its own
The chain's base free joint is commented out, so the forearm and hand are fixed to the hand mount
The only free joint of the scene belongs to the ball body at pos .1 -.1 .25
A weld equality connects the mocap1 body to the forearm body
The position actuators name one joint and an explicit ctrlrange each; A_WRJ1 has ctrlrange -0.52 to 0.17 and kp 50, and A_WRJ0 has ctrlrange -0.79 to 0.61 and kp 50
The Adroit default class sets general actuators to ctrllimited="true" with ctrlrange -1 1
WRJ1 is a hinge joint with range -0.524 to 0.175 rad
THJ0 is a hinge joint with range -1.571 to 0 rad
The tendon section declares fixed tendons from T_WRJ1r to T_THJ0l with ranges
The mesh assets are named with the file paths ../Adroit/resources/meshes/*.stl

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; the bridge takes no seed input and cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults, so a run repeats exactly on the same engine but no seed selects a different state

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the model file for the joint dimensions, the actuator count and the control ranges but integrates a placeholder motion of each actuated hinge toward its control value, so trajectories, contacts, tendons, the weld equality and actuator dynamics are not MuJoCo's

the model comments out its base free joint (resources/chain.xml:14), so the 4-DOF arm described in README.md:6 is not present in this scene: the hand is fixed to the world and the only free body is the ball, whose free-joint dynamics the fake does not integrate

the mesh file paths in resources/assets.xml:34-44 point at ../Adroit/resources/meshes, which does not resolve inside this clone; the fake loads no mesh and the real MuJoCo load of the clone was not run
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine

snapshot and restore use the bridge's fallback copy of time, qpos, qvel and ctrl (the stand-in has no mj_getState), so they are not exact for the contact, tendon and warm-start state of the real engine
no physical Adroit hand or arm is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

measures.name: time_ms

measures.description: Control vector last applied to the actuators (ctrl)
measures.name: ctrl

measures.description: Integration steps since the last reset
measures.name: tick

measures.description: Integration step of the model (null when the model states none)
measures.name: timestep_ms

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
